about.text: Papareireiā is a solar farm on farmland near Maungaturoto in the Kaipara, built to supply Ryman Healthcare's retirement villages under a 10-year agreement. It is a joint venture of Tupu Tonu (the Ngāpuhi Investment Fund), Purpose Capital and Harbour Infrastructure. Ryman's supply is sleeved through Mercury, which tops it up when the sun is low. Construction began in late 2024 and the farm officially went live on 4 December 2025; it is expected to produce about 32 GWh a year. Its name refers to the sun's rays being taken in by the land.

facts.label: Other names
facts.value: Ryman Healthcare Solar Farm, Golden Stairs Solar Farm
facts.note: Golden Stairs Solar Farm: its earlier name, after Golden Stairs Road, Maungaturoto; Transpower's Appendix D still uses it, and the register's unit code is GDS0

facts.label: Commissioned
facts.note: officially went live on 4 December 2025; the developer gives first generation in November 2025 and formal commissioning on 6 January 2026; the register's row starts 13 November 2025. The EA's metered data shows small amounts of output under the farm's code from January 2025, never more than about 330 MWh a month before it went live

facts.label: Owner
facts.value: Tupu Tonu, Purpose Capital and Harbour Infrastructure (joint venture)
facts.note: the register's operator: Maungaturoto Solar Farm Project LP

facts.label: Other ratings
facts.value: 21 MW (the panels' combined peak rating, DC)
